01 / Research experience

Research experience progressing from molecular expression analysis to tumor immunology and, currently, immune regulation in ischemic tissue repair.

Sep 2024 — Present Nankai University

Lower-limb ischemia and immune-mediated tissue repair

★ Primary project
Master’s research · Ongoing

I established the mouse hindlimb ischemia model through lower-limb vascular dissection and ligation, and led ischemic-tissue collection and immune characterization. I used flow cytometry, single-cell transcriptomic analysis, and single-cell TCR sequencing to investigate immune-cell heterogeneity and Treg states. Follow-up work includes CRISPR-based perturbation, molecular assays, and functional validation.

Based on the research experience above, my longer-term interest is to understand how tissue microenvironments shape immune-cell states and how those states influence disease and tissue repair.

05 / Research interests

From tissue injury to repair: understanding how immune cells sense their environment, adapt their functional states, and shape tissue outcomes.

01 — TISSUE CONTEXT

Immune microenvironments

How tissue injury and local inflammatory cues shape immune-cell composition and function.

02 — CELL STATE

Immune-cell plasticity

Defining immune-cell heterogeneity and functional states through single-cell analysis and mechanistic validation.

03 — TISSUE OUTCOME

Tissue repair and regeneration

Investigating how immune regulation influences tissue recovery after injury, including post-ischemic vascular repair.

06 / Research direction

From local immune-cell states to tissue repair and cross-organ coordination: exploring how tissue environments, cell-cell interactions, and systemic immune communication shape recovery.

Doctoral research · 2027/28 entry

How do immune-cell states emerge from tissue interactions, and can local injury coordinate immune responses across organs to shape repair?

A proposed direction for PhD study

01 — CELLULAR STATES

How are immune-cell states established and maintained?

Investigating the regulatory processes underlying immune-cell heterogeneity, functional plasticity, and state transitions.

02 — TISSUE INTERACTIONS

How do immune cells interact with their local tissue environments?

Exploring how local cues and interactions with stromal, vascular, and other immune-cell populations shape immune-cell function in distinct tissue contexts.

03 — CROSS-ORGAN IMMUNITY

Can local injury engage cross-organ immune communication?

Exploring the possibility that local tissue injury induces systemic immune changes or immune-cell trafficking that may influence responses in distant organs.

04 — TISSUE OUTCOMES

How do local and systemic immune responses influence tissue repair?

Understanding how immune regulation contributes to tissue recovery, vascular remodeling, regeneration, and repair-associated outcomes.

Exploratory perspective

Cross-organ immune interaction is presented as a future research possibility rather than an established conclusion, with particular interest in whether localized injury can be accompanied by coordinated immune responses in distant tissues.

Research foundation
Treg biology Ischemic injury Single-cell immunology Tissue repair Cross-organ immune interactions
